summary: Describes the relationship between Internet Protocol addresses and addresses on several specific networks. It also shows the class A, B and C layout of the 32-bit internet address. This RFC is historic.

eli5.summary: Every computer has an internet address, and every network has its own style of local address. This memo is a chart for translating from one to the other.

subtitle: A 1981 chart showing how a 32-bit internet address was split into network and local parts, and how each early network's own addresses fitted inside.

tldr.problem: An internet address has a network number and a local address, but every network has its own address format and length. Gateways needed to know how to turn one into the other.
tldr.mechanism: The memo shows the three address codings (class a, b and c) and then, for each of several networks, draws exactly where that network's native address sits inside the local part of the internet address.
tldr.outcome: The unit metadata lists this RFC as Historic. It is a snapshot of the networks and network numbers of September 1981 and replaces IEN 115.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 796 as Historic, and no RFC is recorded as obsoleting it. It records the network numbers and local networks of September 1981 and replaces IEN 115.

sections.title: Internet Address Codings
sections.content:
This memo describes the relationship between the address fields used in the Internet Protocol (RFC 791) and several specific networks. An internet address is a 32 bit quantity, and it has several codings.

Each coding splits the 32 bits into a network number and a local address. The local address carries the information needed to address a host inside the network that the network number names.
sections.eli5: An internet address is like a street address with two parts: which neighborhood, and which house inside it.

sections.title: Class A, B and C Addresses
sections.content:
The first type, class a, has a 7-bit network number and a 24-bit local address. The address starts with a leading 0 bit.

The second type, class b, has a 14-bit network number and a 16-bit local address, and starts with the bits 1 0. The third type, class c, has a 21-bit network number and an 8-bit local address, and starts with the bits 1 1 0.
sections.eli5: There are three sizes of neighborhood. Some have a huge number of houses, some a medium number and some only a few.

sections.title: Mapping Local Network Addresses
sections.content:
Because each network has its own address format and length, the memo gives a transformation for each one. In every case the network's own address is placed inside the local part of the internet address. All the networks listed are class A.

  • ARPANET (network number 10): 24-bit addresses made of host, logical host and IMP fields are used directly as the 24-bit local address. The IMPs did not yet support logical addressing, so the logical host field is set to zero in the leader.
  • AUTODIN II (26): a 16-bit host or terminal address sits in the low 16 bits, with a zero octet before it.
  • DCNs: 16-bit addresses split into an 8-bit host identifier and an 8-bit process identifier. COMSAT-DCN is network 29 and UCL-DCN is network 30.
  • EDN (21): the same layout as the ARPANET.
  • LCSNET (18): the low order 24 bits of the 32-bit LCS NET address are used, as subnet, reserved and host octets.
  • PRNET: 16-bit addresses, independent of location. Six packet radio networks are listed, with network numbers 1, 2, 5, 6, 9 and 20.
  • SATNET (4): 16-bit logical host addresses, so several can belong to one physical host.
  • WBCNET (28): a 16-bit address split into an 8-bit HAP number and an 8-bit local address.
sections.eli5: Each network gets its own slot in the big address and the memo shows which boxes its own numbers fill, padding the rest with zeros.

sections.title: References and Scope
sections.content: The memo is a plain reference table with no procedures beyond the layouts above. It points to RFC 791 for the Internet Protocol, to a BBN note for the WBCNET address format, and to IEN 82 for the several LCS NET address formats.
sections.eli5: It is only a lookup chart. It tells you where to find more details if you need them.

fields.name: Class bit
fields.desc: A leading zero marks a class a address.

fields.name: Local Address
fields.desc: Addresses a host within the network.
